summary: Full backend + frontend testing for Comment Like feature. All 7 test scenarios from the review request passed. 12 backend pytest tests + 5 Playwright UI tests all green.
passed_tests: BACKEND TEST 1 PASS: GET /api/games/{id}/comments (unauthenticated) returns like_count and liked_by_me fields on every comment
BACKEND TEST 2 PASS: GET /api/games/{id}/comments (authenticated as admin) returns like_count as int and liked_by_me as bool
BACKEND TEST 3 PASS: POST /like without auth returns 401/403 (auth required)
BACKEND TEST 4 PASS: POST /like returns {liked: true}
BACKEND TEST 5 PASS: POST /like is idempotent — second call still returns {liked: true} without error
BACKEND TEST 6 PASS: After POST /like, GET comments shows liked_by_me=True and like_count>=1
BACKEND TEST 7 PASS: like_count is exactly 1 for a fresh newly-created comment
BACKEND TEST 8 PASS: POST /like on nonexistent comment returns 404
BACKEND TEST 9 PASS: DELETE /like returns {liked: false}
BACKEND TEST 10 PASS: After DELETE /like, GET comments shows liked_by_me=False and like_count=0
BACKEND TEST 11 PASS: DELETE /like is idempotent — second call still returns {liked: false}
BACKEND TEST 12 PASS: New comment (just posted) has like_count=0 and liked_by_me=False
FRONTEND TEST 1 PASS: Logged-in admin — every comment has data-testid=like-comment-{id}, clicking it turns heart red and shows count '1' (optimistic update)
FRONTEND TEST 2 PASS: Unlike — clicking red heart again turns it back to empty, count disappears (back to 0)
FRONTEND TEST 3 PASS: Persistence — after closing and reopening comment sheet for same game, the liked comment still shows red heart + count '1' (server state persisted)
FRONTEND TEST 4 PASS: Guest like attempt — clicking heart button as guest shows toast 'Sign in to like comments'
FRONTEND TEST 5 PASS: New comment starts with 0 likes (no count shown), like it → count shows '1'
critical_code_review_comments: No issues found. CommentLike model has UniqueConstraint on (comment_id, user_id) — idempotency handled correctly. Optimistic UI + server revert on failure implemented properly in handleLike(). GET comments batches like_counts and user_liked_ids efficiently in one query each.

Minor note: like_count is only returned via the GET comments batch query; the POST/DELETE /like endpoints do not return the updated count. Frontend relies on optimistic increment/decrement which is correct, but if the server-side count diverges from optimistic state on error, the revert only restores the pre-click count (fine for single user, may be stale for concurrent likes from other users — acceptable for current scope).
